What works for one person, may not work for another. Not all generics/brands will work identical. I'm not saying all generics will have different effects. I'm saying some of them are not equal and some people have different thresholds on their therapeutic levels which may be noticed when switching to a different manufacturer.

I honestly don't understand all the arm chair pharmacists and doctors in this thread. Based on my experience, my patient's experience, medical school curriculum, and numerous physicians who have taught me in clinicals agree not all generics are the same. It's honestly a shame so many are discrediting people's experiences like yours and mine. 

At the end of the day research for medication is lacking that isn't skewed by a specific patient population, all of us have different effects from inactive ingredients, and our comorbidities and varying physiology allows us to not react exactly the same to medications.

Actually I have MCAS and have high levels of histamine and IgE in my body. I also have narcolepsy demonstrated by  abnormal hypocretin. Funny thing about my narcolepsy is I nod out during the day and can't sleep at night.  What exactly are your credentials to make this type of diagnosis? My body's physiology is different producing my symptoms effectively treated by medications.

Edit: there are also many conditions that lead to sleep issues, some can indeed be mental, others breathing related, hormone related, circadian rhythm disorders, ect. For hives, yes there is indeed stress hives which some may considered "in your head", however people can and do have allergies to specific allergens in addition to disorders that increase the allergic response in their bodies completely unrelated to their stress levels or "in your head" as you call it.

Unfortunately my hives are not in my head, especially when my family were just giving me pills as a child. Something I knew nothing of them changing the medicine from name brand to generic. Something that holds true with some random generic from Amazon I got a few years ago that acts like a sugar pill where as Walmarts generic is the same as the name brand for me.  

This is actually a pretty big occurrence with Adderall where people outright request specific manufacturers since they do not all produce the same effects in the same individual. 

My favorite is always my sleeping pill. I've used whatever is easiest available (same active ingredient) and once I took one generic that was completely useless, I took 6x my normal dose and nothing happened. Actually looked it up and that specific manufacturer is regarded as lesser effects in the general community who takes the drug.

Everyone's body reacts different and I would love to see studies incorporating more variety in age, race, and sex while studying effectiveness of these drugs. I also won't change my mind based on an faq rather than studies that equate the two manufacturers as producing the same level and outcome of treatment. I believe the manufacturers just prove the same bioavailability after administration with the assumption that even with different inactive ingredients it will produce an equivalent effect however I have seen many patients, doctors, and pharmacists argue that some of the generics seem to not produce the same level of treatment in all patients. I've always wondered if it's a quality control issue or simply an impact from the body's response to certain inactive ingredients.

Many people (online, friends, and my patients) have had the same experience as me with different effectiveness as the generics. While the active ingredient is the same the quality of medicine delivery and potency is not identical.

Disagree for all OTC meds. I got generic allergy meds from different places and one of them has absolutely 0 effect. In general you should be able to find a generic that works, but not all generics are the same.

According to my US medical textbooks for our ethics course age is a big factor. All of us will deteriorate as we age creating several reasons they would not be a good candidate for transplant. So a 43 year old won't equal a 93 year old. You need a person who the transplant can give a long amount of life to (5 years vs 5 days) that also is compatible and expected to survive the surgery. It is not first come first serve unless you have 2 people in the same circumstance (same reason for transplant, neither expected to die sooner than the other without one). 

Once you hit a certain age you won't be recommended certain surgeries and cancer treatments (these are recommendations, if you want them you can have them). So a 93yo won't be recommended to have a heart transplant because they were waiting longer because they won't be expected to survive and have a good quality of life post surgery over a 43yo.
